summary:
Earth Beat is an interactive web application that transforms Earth science data into music. It allows people to explore our planet through a rotating virtual globe that converts environmental patterns into unique sounds.

The project features nine layers: Lightning, Night Lights, Ocean, Currents, Aerosols, CO₂, Forests, Moisture, and Warming. Users can rotate the globe using a mouse or keyboard and listen to different environmental patterns. The Warming layer uses historical NASA GISTEMP temperature data, while the other layers use simplified representations inspired by NASA scientific visualizations.

Designed especially for blind and low-vision users, Earth Beat makes Earth science more accessible through sound. By combining science, music, and inclusive technology, it offers an innovative way for everyone to experience and understand our changing planet.
details:
Introduction

Earth Beat is an innovative web-based application that converts Earth science information into music, allowing users to hear and explore our planet.

Working Principle

A virtual globe displays Earth with interactive latitude rings. Users can rotate the globe using mouse movements or keyboard arrow keys. The region facing the user determines the musical sounds.

Nine Environmental Layers

  • Lightning – rhythmic clicks representing lightning activity.
  • Night Lights – rising and falling notes representing changes in nighttime brightness.
  • Ocean – sounds representing ocean temperature.
  • Currents – flowing sounds representing major ocean currents.
  • Aerosols – atmospheric particles represented through different sound textures.
  • CO₂ – musical pulses representing yearly carbon dioxide levels.
  • Forests – high-pitched sounds representing forest canopy height.
  • Moisture – flowing sounds representing atmospheric river patterns.
  • Warming – musical notes generated from historical global temperature anomalies.

Technology Used

The project is developed as a single HTML file and runs in a modern web browser without installation or user accounts. It includes interactive globe controls, keyboard navigation, screen-reader descriptions, audio generation, and audio export.

Accessibility and Innovation

Earth Beat is designed especially for blind and low-vision users. Instead of depending only on visual maps, it transforms environmental information into sound. It combines music, technology, science, and inclusive design to make Earth exploration accessible to more people.

Data Accuracy

The Warming layer uses 136 yearly values from NASA GISS GISTEMP historical temperature records from 1880 to 2015. The other eight layers use simplified, manually created representations inspired by NASA Scientific Visualization Studio resources. They are not direct NASA measurements or imagery.

Impact and Future Scope

Earth Beat encourages environmental awareness and makes scientific information easier to experience through sound. Future development includes integrating real NASA gridded datasets into all layers, extending the temperature record, and testing the application with blind and low-vision users.
